item.title: What Trump's flip-flopping on strikes means for the war with Iran
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Mona Yacoubian, director of the Middle East Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, on President Trump's pattern with threatening strikes on Iran.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Mona Yacoubian, director of the Middle East Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, on President Trump's pattern with threatening strikes on Iran.

item.title: With U.S. doors shutting, Cubans turn to Brazil for asylum
item.description: For years, many Cubans hoping to leave the island looked to the United States. Now, with legal pathways largely closed, a growing number are heading to Brazil instead.
item.content:encoded:
For years, many Cubans hoping to leave the island looked to the United States. Now, with legal pathways largely closed, a growing number are heading to Brazil instead.

(Image credit: Ramon Espinosa)

item.title: Todd Blanche rescinds 'anti-weaponization fund'. And, Trump calls off striking Iran
item.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche rescinds President Trump's anti-weaponization fund ahead of his confirmation hearing. And, the president calls off strikes on Iran over a potential deal.

item.title: Rare photos of ex-Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi give her family hope
item.description: Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, told NPR that photographs of his mother meeting a foreign official gave him "a reason to hope" for the first time since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.

item.title: U.S. steps in to help shore up Japanese yen
item.description: The U.S. dollar weakened against the Japanese yen Monday after the leaders of both countries confirmed they intervened in the markets to help shore up Japan's currency.

item.title: Morocco denies responsibility for events at its border with Spain, as deaths near 100
item.description: Four days after tens of thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into the small Spanish territory of Ceuta, the death toll continues to rise -- nearing 100.

item.title: Israel says it has serious concerns with the White House's Hamas disarmament deal
item.description: President Trump announced a proposed disarmament deal with Hamas last week. Israeli strikes overnight and into Sunday evening killed at least 17 people, including children, in Gaza.

item.title: South Korea ditches 'denuclearization-first' strategy. What will Pyongyang do next?
item.description: South Korea is moving away from its policy of prioritizing the immediate denuclearization of North Korea. But despite that shift, experts doubt Pyongyang will return to the negotiating table.

item.title: U.S. dollar weakens sharply against the Japanese yen after market interventions
item.description: The U.S. dollar weakened sharply Monday against the Japanese yen after U.S. President Donald Trump and Japan's finance minister confirmed both sides had intervened in markets.

item.title: A blaze on an Indonesian passenger ferry leaves at least 5 dead and dozens missing
item.description: An Indonesian ferry carrying 271 people has caught fire in waters off Madura island, killing at least five people and leaving 41 others unaccounted for, authorities said
